clue.text: Priest: one entering salutation for religious occasion

indicators.note: the priest and the one go into the middle of the greeting

parts.note: good day is a greeting
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a title for a priest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman joins the congregation's greeting on a feast day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sends the priest and the one into the middle of the greeting, between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friday before Easter is a solemn Christian holy day marking the crucifixion.

clue.text: It follows gulf: a trail going over islands

indicators.note: the whole string turns over, read from the back

parts.note: so means therefore, as in it follows that
a gap is a gulf
to lag is to trail behind

explanation.surface: A path leads round the islands after the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns the whole string SO GAP A LAG back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific archipelago off Ecuador famous for Darwin's finches and giant tortoises.

clue.text: Private happy to confess

parts.note: your own is private to you
up means cheerful

explanation.surface: A soldier is glad to admit something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier but means personal.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit a fault or acknowledge wrongdoing.

clue.text: Tiny grains found seconds after well bursts

indicators.note: the healthy word comes first, the rest after it

parts.note: fit means healthy
sand is made of tiny grains
to found is to start

explanation.surface: Tiny particles are found moments after a well erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' is the definition as a noun: spurts of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular bursts of activity with pauses between them, as spasmodic effort goes.

clue.text: Give protection that's not ingested in hormone

indicators.note: the eating word is removed from the protecting verb

parts.note: to insulate is to shield or protect
ate means took in as food
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hormone protects against something that hasn't been swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes ATE out of INSULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreatic hormone regulating blood sugar, lacking in diabetes.

clue.text: Fruit and eggs to lift roughly and bash

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting reads the word upwards

parts.note: ova are eggs
CA is circa, roughly
a do or a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A cook lifts fruit and eggs and hits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns OVA upwards in this down clue to AVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped green fruit with a large stone and buttery flesh.

clue.text: Pair meeting for a snap appearing in picture

definitions.meaning: the upper and lower bones of a mouth come together to bite

explanation.surface: Two parts snapping shut in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony parts of the mouth that bite, and also the title of a famous shark film.

clue.text: Suddenly, when caught breaking and entering, there's universal penance

parts.note: all means everyone, universal

indicators.note: the caught letter gets inside the atonement word

parts.note: to atone is to do penance
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A burglar caught in the act is made to do penance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking and entering' is a burglary phrase here putting C inside ATONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening at one moment without warning, all of a sudden.

clue.text: Tips from customers in bistro go round in pouch

indicators.note: the tips here are the ends of each word, the final letters

explanation.surface: Diners leave gratuities in a small bag passed round the bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' suggests gratuities; here it takes the end of each of five words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet bag that holds the back hair, a small netted pouch.

clue.text: Was our joiner taking this medicine by mouth?

indicators.note: said by mouth, the words are heard rather than read; also how this syrup is taken

parts.note: something that was our joiner linked us

explanation.surface: A question about whether a carpenter took a dose of medicine orally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mouth' does double duty in the surface: cough syrup is taken orally, and the indicator says the phrase 'linked us' is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick syrupy cough medicine swallowed to soothe the throat.

clue.text: He opposed the Turkish brothel local keeps

indicators.note: the run of words holds the name within it, the two words keeping it

explanation.surface: A man who fought against a Turkish bordello kept by the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moor of Shakespeare's play commands Venice's forces against the Turks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moorish general leads the Venetian fleet against the Ottoman Turks in Cyprus.

clue.text: Entirely sound group of faculties in general service

indicators.note: the word for entirely is said aloud

parts.note: wholly means entirely

indicators.note: the university goes inside the general word

parts.note: common means general or shared
a university is made up of faculties, uni for short

explanation.surface: A whole body of academic departments attends a general service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy but signals a word heard aloud; 'in general' reads as a phrase meaning generally, but sets the university inside the word for general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist, the Christian service of bread and wine.

clue.text: Better just quietly answer her

parts.note: to pip is to beat narrowly
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone is told to outdo a quiet reply from a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is the definition: any girl's name fits, here a short one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippa is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as her.

clue.text: Van going about fifty feet sorted and dropped fliers

indicators.note: the verb for leading goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to be in the van is to lead

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A delivery vehicle travelled about fifty feet while its crew distributed pamphlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle but is the front of an army, hence leading. 'sorted' rearranges fifty and the feet, and 'going about' places the leading verb round them, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaflet is to hand out printed sheets, so the past tense means dropped fliers.

clue.text: Way with water shown in posh wedding where wine miraculously transformed by litre!

parts.note: grand means posh or upmarket
a union is a marriage
Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding

explanation.surface: At a smart wedding, the water was miraculously turned into wine, measured by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reverses the miracle. The answer is a long English canal linking London and Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a waterway, a route that carries water instead of a road surface.

clue.text: Equipment getting hot has staff frantically ringing alarms

indicators.note: the rearranged staff letters surround the other pieces
the letters move about in a frenzy

parts.note: taken as written
a rig is equipment
H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

explanation.surface: Gear heating up sends staff into a panic as alarms ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges the staff letters into AFFTS, and 'ringing' wraps that round the equipment and the hot letter; 'alarms' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To affright is to frighten, so it means scares or alarms.

clue.text: Lechery rebuked and ritually cleansed

parts.note: lust is lechery
to rate is to scold

explanation.surface: Lustful behaviour was scolded and the sinner purified by ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to purify by ceremonial washing or sacrifice.

clue.text: Company's security policy

parts.note: read not as a firm's security rules but as the idea that being in company keeps one safe

explanation.surface: A business's rules on protecting its premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb meaning that being one of a large group protects you from harm.

clue.text: Established Church following one plan for renewal

indicators.note: the Church letters come after the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters are made over anew

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The established Church follows a single plan for renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for renewal' rearranges the one and the plan into INPLA; 'following' puts the Church letters after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something established is set up and settled where it belongs.

clue.text: Nearly drop off and finally land on the French beans

parts.note: to nod is to almost fall asleep

indicators.note: it takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: les is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone nods off, finally lands, and is served French beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beans' looks like vegetables but is slang for heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle and bean are both informal words for the head.

clue.text: Did impression of winger's run, hip cured, amazingly

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into an amazing new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer's run, now that his hip is healed, is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a football wide player, but here it is a bird. 'amazingly' rearranges R, HIP and CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirruping is the short shrill call of a bird, so to chirrup is to imitate a winged creature's sound.

clue.text: Teacher's stick the cause of some white faces?

definitions.meaning: the stick teachers write on boards with

definitions.text: the cause of some white faces
definitions.meaning: the soft white rock of cliffs such as Dover's

explanation.surface: A teacher's stick causes pale faces among pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft white limestone used for blackboard sticks and forming white cliff faces.

clue.text: Steer with this? Not right!

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: a rudder is what a boat is steered with

explanation.surface: A question about a ship's steering, met with a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, a steer is a castrated bull, so a steer with a teat bag is plainly not right.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk gland of a cow, which a male steer should not have.

clue.text: Alas back away from healthy snack, finding rum

indicators.note: the turned letters are removed from the snack

parts.note: a salad roll is a wholesome snack

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone backs away from a healthy snack, finding drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALAS into SALA, and 'away from' takes it off SALAD ROLL. 'rum' is the old adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum and droll both mean odd or comically strange.

clue.text: A power is like wizard's (but not magician's) spell: it renders one speechless

annotationWithheld.clue: A power is like wizard's (but not magician's) spell: it renders one speechless

clue.text: Dispatched boxer perhaps, spent

definitions.meaning: to lay out money is to spend it

explanation.surface: A fighter is knocked down and exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocked-down fighter is floored flat, and money that has been paid is outlaid.

clue.text: Something applied to lips after make-up?

definitions.text: Something applied to lips after make-up?

parts.words: Something applied to lips after make-up?
parts.note: make-up looks like cosmetics, but it is making up after a quarrel, sealed with the lips

explanation.surface: A cosmetic, like lip balm, put on after foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples kiss and make up, so a kiss is pressed on the lips when a row ends.

clue.text: A pair of boys penning a brief newspaper item

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per day

indicators.note: the two boys enclose the letter between them

parts.note: a son and a lad are two boys
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Two lads write a short piece for the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing: the two boys close round the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: A short notice placed in a paper's classified columns, often seeking a partner.
